question: Will the UN act on Yemen's claim, yes or no?

lines.text: Yemen's government says 21 experts from Iran's Revolutionary Guards and Hezbollah are directing Houthi operations.
Minister Ibrahim Haidan says fourteen are IRGC and seven are Hezbollah.
He says support has moved from training to direct supervision.
Haidan said: This is not a training mission, but a fully fledged general staff.

scene.quote: This is not a training mission, but a fully fledged general staff

lines.text: The ministry says eight of them are in the Red Sea port of Hodeidah.
Four each are in Sanaa and Saada, the rest in Hajjah, Amran and Khokha.
It lists ballistic missiles, drones, and choosing commercial ships as targets among their skills.
Haidan warned this threatens shipping in the Bab al Mandeb strait and the Red Sea.
The ministry did not name the 21 or provide evidence, The National says.
Tehran insists the Houthis act independently, and Hezbollah denies a role in Yemen, Al Jazeera says.
Four military sources told Reuters on Monday the Houthis are within 80 kilometres of Aden.
The Houthis say they targeted Saudi Arabia's Abha airport and an air base on Tuesday.
Haidan wants the Houthis listed as a terrorist group. Will the UN act on Yemen's claim, yes or no?

notes_full: First reported 3 Nov about 11:45 UTC (South24), The National 15:52, Arab News 16:36, L'Orient 17:10, Al Jazeera 19:13, Asharq Al-Awsat 19:30; about 9h old at delivery
All expert claims framed as Yemen's Interior Ministry / Haidan; no evidence given (The National); Iran and Hezbollah denials included (Al Jazeera)
80 km from Aden: Reuters 4 military sources, 2 Nov, via The National 3 Nov (context)
Abha / Khamis Mushait: Houthi military spokesperson claim 3 Nov 13:15 UTC (MTV Lebanon), also Pakistan Today, Breakingthenews; framed as Houthi claim
Removal-risk: attributed claims and events; no death toll; no future-attack framing; neutral yes/no on UN action
